_note: Admin changelog entries. Written by Claude from each commit's message, file list and size (git supplies the date, author and size). Add new entries at the top; the server inserts any new commit hash on boot and never overwrites an existing row. See docs/changelog.md.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Sketchbook: say plainly why a draw failed, and whether it was charged
entries.goal: A first live attempt failed with a message saying nothing was charged. That claim covered every failure, including one after the picture was drawn and paid for, and it hid the real reason (a 404 from the image service).
entries.whatChanged: Draw and Change now separate two failures. Image service failed: the message gives the likely reason (no FAL key, graphics model not usable, 404 meaning the model set in Settings is not a FAL model name, out of credit or locked, timeout, blocked) and says no spend was recorded. Picture came back but could not be saved: the message says the person may have been charged and to check Usage (feature graphics_sketchbook). Provider text is still logged and never shown. Tests cover each message.
entries.benefit: The person is told the real reason and is never told money was not spent when it may have been. The 404 case points at the Settings fix.
entries.concerns: The reason is picked by matching words in the provider error, so an unusual error still gets the generic line (plus "no spend recorded", which holds for any failure before a picture returns). The 404 wording is a best reading: the cause on the live site is not confirmed until the graphics model in Settings is checked. Does not fix the 404 itself; that is a Settings value.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Add Sketchbook: describe a scene, get a cartoon you can change later
entries.goal: Turn a described scene, theory or possibility into a cartoon, keep a collection of them, and let the person change the same picture later with more instructions, in pencil, coloured pens or coloured in. It is a separate tool from Graphics because it is project-shaped (saved collection, history, follow-up edits) while Graphics tools are one picture in, one picture out.
entries.whatChanged: New Sketchbook tool at /sketchbook and /sketchbook/:id (Content Creation). Describe a scene by typing or speaking, choose Pencil, Pen (7 ink colours) or Coloured in and a shape, and the image model draws it. Each sketch is saved; Change this picture changes the same sketch and keeps the last 6 earlier pictures with their look; Put back restores one (and the picture it replaced is kept); Colour it in redraws in colour; PNG, JPG, WebP and Copy picture. Collection with search, rename, copy and delete into the recycle bin with Undo. New table sketches, recycle bin adapter (type sketch), 11 API routes under /api/sketchbook behind the sketchbook flag (default off, preview), 11 route manifest entries. Reuses the Graphics image generation, paid-tool guard, daily cost cap (usage feature graphics_sketchbook) and content restrictions. New how-it-works box; docs/sketchbook.md and a key-files entry.
entries.benefit: Pictures of ideas and scenarios without drawing skill, kept in one private collection that can be reopened and refined, with no new image provider setup and the existing spending limits already applied.
entries.concerns: Not tried with the live image service: the screens and flow were checked in a browser against a stand-in that draws simple shapes, so how well the default FAL edit model (fal-ai/flux-kontext/dev, env SKETCHBOOK_EDIT_MODEL) follows instructions on cartoons, and its price (estimated 3 cents, env SKETCHBOOK_EDIT_COST_USD), are unproven. On a local copy a change can only nudge the picture (ComfyUI image to image). Each draw or change is a paid call and shares the daily image limit with Graphics. Switched off for members until an admin turns it on. Pictures are stored in the database (up to ~6 MB per sketch with its earlier pictures, 200 sketches per person). Not built: Copy to Notes, hand drawing, comic strips and consistent characters, guide chat and tour, SVG/PDF export. crossUser.test.js still fails on 11 older SERP Tracker routes missing from the manifest (not part of this commit). No package.json change, so the deploy should be fast.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Rename the Drawings tool to Diagrams (display names only)
entries.goal: The tool had become a flowcharting and diagramming tool (Draw it for me, loops, shape numbers, What have I missed?), so Drawings no longer described it.
entries.whatChanged: Renamed to Diagrams in everything a person sees: the menu and sidebar entry and page heading, the Feature Access label, the guide chat (Diagrams guide), the tour, help box and tooltips, New diagram / Your diagrams, the default title Untitled diagram, the recycle bin label, error messages, and the wording of notes made from it (From the diagram ...). Internal names are unchanged: the drawings feature flag, /drawings URL, /api/drawings routes, drawings table, customData keys, file names and the guide key. Notes still link back by their ](/drawings/N) link. The Ctrl+K aliases now include drawing, sketch, whiteboard and flowchart. docs/drawings.md and CLAUDE.md note the rename.
entries.benefit: The name says what the tool is for, and matches Excalidraw-style whiteboard users and flowchart users alike through the search aliases.
entries.concerns: Existing drawings keep their old default title (Untitled drawing) and existing notes keep From the drawing, since only new items use the new words. The rename was done with a script over the text people see; a first pass also changed SQL table names inside the code, which a test caught and was reverted before commit, and the remaining visible screens were checked for leftover words on the list page and editor only, not every message, guide answer or error. The board's own tooltips still say drawing (Excalidraw's text). The stored default title and the guide name change for everyone at once, including anyone who knew it as Drawings.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Drawings: remove duplicate Undo/Redo buttons from the board's top right
entries.goal: Remove a duplicate: the Undo and Redo buttons added in the board's top right only clicked the board's own arrows at its bottom left.
entries.whatChanged: Removed the Undo / Redo buttons from renderBoardTools, the canUndo / canRedo state and the 400 ms polling that kept them in step with the board. The board's own Undo / Redo arrows (bottom left) remain, and Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z still work through handleKeyboardGlobally. Guide chat, tour and docs/drawings.md now point to the bottom-left arrows.
entries.benefit: One fewer duplicate control on a crowded screen, and no polling timer running while a drawing is open.
entries.concerns: The board's own Undo / Redo arrows are small. Checked on screen that one press removes a whole generated diagram and Redo then becomes available; the keyboard shortcuts were not exercised.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Drawings: move Undo/Redo, Keep shape/Free and Select all into the board
entries.goal: Declutter the bar above the drawing board by putting the board's own controls inside the drawing area.
entries.whatChanged: Undo / Redo, Keep shape / Free and Select all moved from the bar above the board into the board's top right, beside the Library button, using Excalidraw's renderTopRightUI (renderBoardTools in DrawingEditor.jsx). The bar above keeps Fit to screen, Snap to grid and Numbers. The board defines its own --color-primary and related variables inside itself, so Vault's values are read from the page root and set on the wrapper to keep the buttons in Vault's colours. Guide chat, tour and docs/drawings.md say where the controls now are.
entries.benefit: A shorter top bar, with the editing controls next to the tools they act on.
entries.concerns: Checked on screen at one screen width only. The wrapper has a maximum width and wraps, but on a narrow window the controls could crowd the board's own tool row. A stretch drag was not re-tested after the move (Keep shape state and Undo/Redo/Select all were). The Vault colours are read when the controls render, so a theme change shows after the next board redraw.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Drawings: shape numbers and "What have I missed?"
entries.goal: Let the owner refer to a shape by number when asking for changes on a busy drawing, and have the AI point out what a diagram may be missing.
entries.whatChanged: New Numbers button shows a small number on each box, diamond and oval that has writing in it. The number is saved in the box's customData.vaultNo and kept; the badges are an HTML overlay on the board, so they never print or export (PNG, SVG, file, Notes). New shapeNumbers.mjs: a box put in between two numbered boxes gets a sub-number of the one before (4.1, then 4.2); anything else gets the next whole number; a copied box with a repeated number gets its own. Numbers are given when the toggle is on, before Change it and What have I missed?, and for boxes the AI adds. The diagram JSON carries a num per node and the prompt tells the AI to copy every num and never invent one, so changes can refer to shapes (add a step after 7). New What have I missed? button in the Draw it for me box: POST /api/drawings/suggestions (askSuggestions in drawingDiagram.js, AI rate limit, usage feature drawing_diagram) sends only the diagram structure and returns up to six suggestions naming shapes by number; Add this makes the change through Change it, Dismiss hides one; nothing changes until Add this. Guide chat, help text, tour, tooltips, docs/drawings.md and routeManifest.json updated.
entries.benefit: On a drawing with many shapes a change or a gap can be pointed at by number, and the AI can raise gaps the owner had not thought of.
entries.concerns: Checked on screen only with a stand-in AI, never a real model: how useful and accurate the suggestions are, and whether a real model keeps shape numbers when changing a diagram, is unproven. The overlay badges are repositioned on every board change, which is fine for a few dozen shapes and unmeasured for hundreds. A number freed by deleting a shape is not reused within a visit, but after a drawing is reopened a freed top number can be reused. Only a box put in between two numbered boxes gets a sub-number; branches and additions at either end take whole numbers. Each What have I missed? press is one AI request. Separately, crossUser.test.js reports 11 SERP Tracker routes missing from routeManifest.json; those are not Drawings routes and were not changed here.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Drawings: change any diagram by voice, waiting steps loop back
entries.goal: Let the owner change an existing drawing by voice (insert, add at the start or end), not only the diagram the AI drew a moment ago, and make waiting steps (a deposit not paid) loop back to the earlier step dependably.
entries.whatChanged: New client/src/pages/drawings/sceneDiagram.mjs (readDiagram) reads a diagram back out of the drawing: boxes with bound writing (rectangle = box, diamond = decision, ellipse = start/end) and arrows bound at both ends, with labels and two-way heads. Change it now uses that instead of the structure remembered from the last AI run, so it works on hand-made diagrams and ones from earlier visits, and reflects hand edits; the diagram containing the selection is used, otherwise the biggest, over 40 boxes is refused. The pieces read are deleted and the updated diagram drawn at their top left (one Undo reverts). The Change it box shows whenever a diagram is readable; Start fresh was removed. The AI prompt now describes insert / add at start / add at end / rename / remove / loop back, and says a step that must wait (payment, approval, reply) is a Yes/No decision whose No arrow loops back to the earlier step. Guide chat, help text and docs/drawings.md updated.
entries.benefit: Diagrams can be extended or corrected by voice at any time, including older and hand-made ones, and processes that must wait for something loop back instead of moving on.
entries.concerns: Seen working on screen only with a stand-in AI (reload, then add a step after the visit); never with a real model, so how well the model inserts steps or draws the deposit loop from real wording is unproven. Boxes moved by hand inside the diagram are laid out again on a change. Arrows from outside a replaced diagram that were bound to its boxes become unattached. Reading a diagram relies on writing being bound inside boxes (the board's normal behaviour), so loose text next to a box is not read. Several diagrams on one drawing rely on selecting a box to choose; otherwise the biggest is used.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Drawings: tidy top row (Draw it for me to More tools, one Notes button, Select all, Fit to screen)
entries.goal: Declutter the Drawings top row, and add the Select all and Fit to screen controls the owner asked for.
entries.whatChanged: Draw it for me left the top row and is now an item in the board's own More tools menu (Generate section, AI tag), added with Excalidraw's TTDDialogTrigger child component; when the board opens its built-in text-to-diagram dialog for that item, onChange closes it at once and opens the existing Draw it for me panel. To Notes and In a note are merged into one button: To Notes when the drawing is in no note; otherwise In a note / In N notes opening a list of Go to each note plus Put in another note. The Two-way arrow button was removed (the board's Arrowheads panel sets both ends). New Select all (selects every live element) and Fit to screen (scrollToContent fitToViewport, zooms in or out) buttons. Guide chat catalog, help text, tour and docs/drawings.md updated.
entries.benefit: A shorter, less congested top row, one notes button instead of two, and easier resizing of whole drawings.
entries.concerns: The More tools entry relies on Excalidraw's TTDDialogTrigger and on its dialog state names (openDialog ttd, tab text-to-diagram); an Excalidraw upgrade could break it, in which case the board's own dialog would show instead. Checked on screen that the item appears, opens our panel and the board dialog does not show. The To Notes to In a note swap after saving a note was not re-run on screen after the merge. Select all and Fit to screen were seen working; the final fit margin (85%) was set after the check and not looked at.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Drawings: undo/redo, keep shape, two-way arrows, loop routing, snap to grid
entries.goal: Act on the owner's feedback after first real use of Draw it for me: stretch everything without bending it, two-way arrows, loops in decision flows, snap to grid, and a multi-step undo/redo.
entries.whatChanged: Undo and Redo buttons above the board drive the board's own unlimited history (a whole generated diagram is one step); Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z work anywhere on the page. Keep shape / Free (remembered) decides whether dragging a corner keeps proportions, with a real Shift doing the opposite for one drag, by overriding the shift state on pointer events during a stretch. Two-way arrow button for selected arrows; Draw it for me may now return two-way edges and merges an arrow each way between two boxes into one. Loop arrows are routed round the outside of the diagram with sharp corners, leaving from underneath when a box sits beside the source, never crossing a box; decision diamonds are larger so text stays on one line. Snap to grid toggles the board's grid, saved with the drawing. Guide chat catalog, help text, tour, tooltips and docs/drawings.md updated.
entries.benefit: Diagrams can be resized, edited and corrected without redrawing; loops and two-way relationships read clearly; boxes line up; mistakes are easy to step back from.
entries.concerns: Tested on screen only with a stand-in AI, never a real model. Keep shape relies on overriding event.shiftKey, which depends on Excalidraw internals and may need rework when the library is upgraded; verified with Select all on a drag-box selection, not on single boxes or pictures. Snap to grid was confirmed by button state and saved setting, not by dragging a box. Ctrl+Z shortcuts were not exercised; only the buttons were. Undo history is per visit and is not saved. Undo/Redo buttons read the board's own button state every 400 ms.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Drawings: Draw it for me (dictate or type a scenario, the AI develops a diagram)
entries.goal: Let a person dictate (or type) a scenario and have a diagram developed from it, instead of drawing every box and arrow by hand.
entries.whatChanged: New Draw it for me button above the drawing board. A panel takes a scenario said into the microphone or typed (the shared dictation text box), and Draw it adds the diagram to the open drawing as ordinary Excalidraw pieces, below anything already there (top left of the screen on an empty drawing), in the look the drawing is in; the panel closes and the board zooms to fit without zooming a small diagram in; one press of the board's Undo removes the whole diagram. A Change it box (say what to change) redraws the last diagram in the same place, replacing the pieces it made earlier (found by a run tag in their customData) and leaving anything drawn by hand around it; Start fresh forgets it; the diagram to change is kept for the visit only. New route POST /api/drawings/diagram (behind the AI rate limit and the drawings flag): one call on the workspace standard model asks for ONLY a structure (kind flow / org / mind map / timeline / relationship, direction, boxes with a short label and shape box / decision / start-end, and arrows with optional labels), never positions. The reply is untrusted and is checked and cleaned (safe unique ids, short labels, known shapes, arrows only between boxes that exist, up to 40 boxes and 80 arrows; unusable replies give a plain message, never raw model text); the person's words are fenced so they cannot pass for instructions. Only the words typed or said are sent, never any drawing; usage is logged as drawing_diagram. The layout is ours (layers by longest path, loops tolerated, boxes sized to wrapped labels, arrows bound to box edges) and goes through Excalidraw's convertToExcalidrawElements. Guide, help box, tour, tooltips, key-files and docs/drawings.md updated. No new package.
filesImpacted: server/services/drawingDiagram.js (new: prompt, checking, ask) and drawingDiagram.test.js
client/src/pages/drawings/DrawingEditor.jsx (button, panel, placing and replacing a diagram)
client/src/pages/drawings/drawingsTools.mjs, server/services/drawingsTutor.js and its test, client/src/utils/tours/drawingsTour.js (guide, help, tour)
entries.benefit: A scenario said or typed becomes a tidy editable diagram in seconds, in the person's own look, and it can be adjusted by saying what to change.
entries.concerns: NOT TRIED WITH A REAL MODEL: there is no AI key locally, so the screen was checked with a stand-in that returns fixed diagrams (a flow with a decision, an org chart, a change that adds a box), including the Clean look, a reload and Undo. How good the boxes are from real descriptions, how long a call takes, and whether the 4,000-character and 40-box limits suit real use are unknown. Dictation by microphone was not tried (typing was). Costs one AI request per Draw it or Change it (logged in Usage as drawing_diagram), behind the existing AI rate limit. Flows, org charts, mind maps, timelines and relationship diagrams only: not drawings to scale (floor plans), illustrations, or reading or tidying a drawing the person made. A change replaces the last diagram including any hand edits to it, and cannot be made after the drawing has been closed. The keyboard Ctrl+Z sent by the browser-automation tool did not reach the board while the on-screen Undo button worked (probably the tool, not the app; not proven). Not run on Railway. No package change, so a normal fast deploy.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Drawings: In a note button on each card in the list
entries.goal: Show on the list of drawings which drawings are in notes, as the drawing editor already does, so the way back to a note does not need the drawing to be opened first.
entries.whatChanged: Each card in Your drawings now shows an In a note button (In N notes when there are several) when notes link back to that drawing; a drawing in no note shows nothing. One note goes straight to it; several open a short list of titles under the card's buttons (fetched when clicked). GET /api/drawings now adds noteCount to every row, worked out in ONE query over the person's notes that mention "/drawings/" (regexp_matches on the "](/drawings/N)" links), not one search per drawing; a note that links twice counts once, and another person's notes never count. Guide wording, help text and docs updated; tests cover the counts (including 7 versus 70 and another person).
filesImpacted: client/src/pages/drawings/DrawingsList.jsx (the button and list on each card)
entries.benefit: From the list you can see at a glance which drawings are in notes and jump to the note with one click.
entries.concerns: The note count is found from the link text in each note, so a note whose link was edited out, or that was deleted, stops counting; a note that merely holds the same Markdown link counts. One pattern-match query runs over the person's notes every time the list opens: fine at normal note counts, not measured on a very large notes table. Tried on screen locally with drawings in no note, one note and two notes (the one-note and two-note paths both opened the right note); not tried on Railway. No package change, so a normal fast deploy.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Drawings: In a note button (go from a drawing to the notes it was sent to)
entries.goal: A drawing that has been sent to a note had no way back to that note (the note links to the drawing, not the other way round).
entries.whatChanged: The drawing editor now shows an In a note button beside To Notes whenever the drawing has been sent to a note: with one note it goes straight to it, with several it reads In N notes and shows a short list of titles (newest first) to choose from. Anything waiting is saved before leaving, as for Your drawings. It appears straight after To Notes without a reload. New route GET /api/drawings/:id/notes finds the signed-in person's notes whose text contains the link To Notes writes, "](/drawings/ID)" (matched with the closing bracket, so drawing 7 never matches drawing 70), newest change first, at most 20; another person's drawing is "not found". No new table: the note's own text is the record, so notes made earlier already work, a note the person linked by hand counts, and deleting a note or removing its link makes the button go away. Guide, help text, docs and tests updated.
filesImpacted: client/src/pages/drawings/DrawingEditor.jsx (the button and list, reloaded after To Notes)
server/services/drawings.test.js (a notes table in the scratch schema; exact matching, another person, 404s)
entries.benefit: You can go from a drawing to the note it is in with one click, matching the existing link from the note back to the drawing.
entries.concerns: Found by the note's link text, not a stored relationship: if the link line is edited out of the note, or the note is deleted, the button stops listing it; a note that merely contains the same Markdown link counts. Capped at 20 notes. Tried on screen locally with one note and with two (opened the right note each time); not tried on Railway, and not tried on a drawing with many notes. The list of drawings does not show it (open the drawing first). A LIKE search over the person's notes runs when a drawing opens: fine at normal note counts, not measured on a very large notes table. No package change, so a normal fast deploy.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Drawings: Sketch / Clean look (reversible), To Notes with the picture shown inside the note
entries.goal: Let a drawing be flipped between the hand-drawn look and a more conservative one in Vault's own colours, and let a drawing be copied into Notes in the way other tools save to Notes, with the picture shown inside the note.
entries.whatChanged: Drawings: two buttons above the board, Sketch and Clean. Clean makes steady straight lines, square corners, straight arrows, solid fills instead of hatching, a plain font (Excalidraw Helvetica family) and Vault's text colour in place of Excalidraw's default black (light themes only). Colours the person chose, freehand pen strokes and pictures are not changed. It is reversible: each piece remembers how it was drawn in its own customData, so Sketch restores exactly what was drawn (checked through three round trips) and Undo works; new pieces start in the drawing's look. The look is stored per drawing (new column drawings.look, added with ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS) and shown on each card in the list. A Pictures choice (same / clean / sketch) changes only the exported PNG or SVG and the Notes picture, never the drawing; the .excalidraw file is always the drawing as it is. New To Notes button: makes a new note named after the drawing (optionally filed under a project or client, as in YouTube), attaches a PNG, and writes a marker line {picture:N} plus a link back to the drawing into the note, using only existing Notes routes. Notes Preview now shows a {picture:N} line as the attached picture (written like the existing {task:N} marker, so the note stays plain text and Write, Rich, search, Ask and the recycle bin keep it as it is); click opens it full size. Drawings guide, help box, tour step, tooltips and docs updated; Notes guide, (i) box and a tip mention the picture. No new package.
filesImpacted: client/src/pages/drawings/lookConvert.mjs (new: Sketch to Clean and back) and its test
client/src/pages/drawings/saveDrawingToNotes.mjs (new: the three Notes steps) and its test
client/src/pages/drawings/DrawingEditor.jsx (look switch, Pictures choice, To Notes panel, look in the save fingerprint)
client/src/pages/notes/notePictures.mjs, NotePicture.jsx, NoteMarkdownView.jsx (picture marker shown in Preview) and notePictures.test.mjs
server/db.js, server/services/drawings.js, server/routes/drawings.js (look column and checks)
server/services/drawingsTutor.js, drawingsTools.mjs, drawingsTour.js and tests (guide, help, tour)
entries.benefit: Drawings can be made tidy and conservative for documents and flipped back to the sketch style without losing anything, and a drawing can go into a note in one step, shown inside the note.
entries.concerns: Not run on Railway. Tried by hand in the local app: Clean and back on a five-piece drawing (restored values checked against the saved scene), a reload keeping Clean, To Notes, the note in Preview and an edit in Rich keeping the marker, and the Pictures choice (clean and same gave identical PNGs, sketch a hatched one, the drawing unchanged). Not tried: drawing a new piece by mouse in the clean look (the starting settings were seen in the tool panel only), a very large drawing (conversion time), the same drawing in two tabs while switching, the guide's real answers (need a model key). Limits by design: the board cannot use Vault's DM Sans or any CSS font; line colour only follows the Vault theme in light themes; existing arrows become straight, not right-angled; converting a drawing from the list without opening it is not built. To Notes makes a new note each time and later drawing changes are not copied; a note shows the picture inside only in Preview (Write and Rich show the marker line {picture:N}, to be left as it is); if the picture is removed from the note a quiet line replaces it. Clean changes text sizes slightly because the font changes; text is re-measured once fonts load. The route inventory test still fails for 11 SERP Tracker routes from other work, not these. No package change, so a normal fast deploy.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Drawings: saved Excalidraw drawings per person (new tool, off by default; adds @excalidraw/excalidraw)
entries.goal: Give Vault a drawing tool: sketches, diagrams and plans on an endless page, saved to the person's account, by embedding the real Excalidraw editor (MIT licence) instead of building one.
entries.whatChanged: New tool Drawings at /drawings (list) and /drawings/:id (one drawing), under Content Creation. The list shows each saved drawing with a small preview, name, piece count and last change, with New drawing, Open a file (an .excalidraw file becomes a new drawing), search by name (with the microphone), Rename, Copy and Delete (inline Delete? Yes / No, an Undo toast, and the shared recycle bin keeps it 30 days). A drawing opens on the Excalidraw editor, loaded only when one is opened, with its fonts served from our own origin (a Vite plugin, like the OCR assets). It saves by itself 1.5 s after the last change and again on leaving, refuses a save from a stale tab (409, ask to reload), and exports PNG, SVG or an .excalidraw file to the person's computer. Excalidraw's own menu is cut down (its collaboration, paid-plan and social links are not shown). New table drawings (scene as TEXT up to 6 MB, preview, counts), routes at /api/drawings behind the new drawings flag, recycle-bin adapter, Drawings guide (/api/drawings-tutor), (i) box, 6-step tour (also in Settings), tooltips and the microphone on the name and search boxes, navigation entry, docs/drawings.md and notes in key-files, schema-notes and guide-chat docs. The flag is OFF by default and marked preview; admins can always open it. Adds the npm package @excalidraw/excalidraw.
filesImpacted: package.json and package-lock.json (adds @excalidraw/excalidraw; npm also deduped a few @floating-ui versions in the lock file)
server/config/featureAccess.js and client/src/utils/featureAccess.js (flag drawings, preview, off)
client/src/pages/DrawingsPage.jsx and client/src/pages/drawings/ (list, editor, helpers, guide wrapper, loader)
client/vite/excalidrawAssets.mjs and client/vite.config.js (fonts from our own origin)
entries.benefit: A proper sketching and diagram tool inside Vault with private, autosaved drawings, undo for deletes and export to PNG, SVG or file, with no editor code to maintain.
entries.concerns: SLOW DEPLOY: package.json and package-lock.json changed, so Railway rebuilds the image from the root npm install onwards (docs/deploy-speed.md); this was accepted before the push. Not run on Railway: memory, first-load time and font loading there are unmeasured, and the editor adds about 5 MB of script that loads only when a drawing is opened. In production mode the security policy blocks one thing, Excalidraw's font-compression helper (it builds code with eval); drawing, saving and all three exports still work, but exported SVG fonts are probably embedded whole; accepted, the policy is not loosened. A data-loss bug was found and fixed before this commit: leaving a drawing saved an empty page over the real one because the editor is already torn down by then; saves now use the last scene the editor reported. Tried locally by hand: new, draw, rename, leave and reopen, copy, delete and Undo, import a file, the three exports, the tour, the guide button (its real answers need a model key and were not tried). Not tried: large pictures, thousands of pieces, a phone, two tabs on screen (the 409 guard is tested on the server only), working offline. Off by default for members until an admin switches it on. No sharing, no live co-editing, no sending into Graphics, Notes or Chat. The route inventory test still fails for 11 SERP Tracker routes from other work, not these.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Video Tools: fold Animated title into Title card (animated look, on a video or as a separate clip)
entries.goal: Remove the overlap between the new Animated title tool (a standalone title clip) and Title card: they were almost the same tool, and a standalone clip alone had little use.
entries.whatChanged: Animated title is no longer its own tool in Make. Title card has a Look choice: Standard card (unchanged) or Animated title, and for the animated look a Show it choice: On my video, or As a separate title clip. On my video lays the animated title over the person's video between a start and an end time (same timeline and times as the standard card); the video keeps its length and its sound is copied; the picture can be darkened behind the title (0 to 80 percent, chosen colour). entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Graphics Brand Kit: read a website's colours, fonts, corners and logo (server reader)
entries.goal: Let Graphics learn a brand (colours, fonts, corners, logo) from any public website, as the first step of filling the Brand Kit from a URL.
entries.whatChanged: New server reader: opens one public page in the Chromium the Browser Agent already uses (desktop, phone and dark-mode looks) and proposes colour roles, heading and body fonts as plain TTF/OTF files, a corner style and logo candidates. Colours are weighted by how much of the page they cover, with cookie bars and sale banners damped. Font files seen on the page are converted from woff2 with fontTools (already installed), cut to one weight if variable, and renamed to a unique plain name so sharp draws exactly the file's outlines; Google Fonts is the fall-back. Every request the page makes, including every redirect leg, is checked with checkSsrf through the browser's request-pause protocol. Nothing is exposed or saved yet.
entries.benefit: A real reading of a site's look instead of a guess, with no new dependency and no Dockerfile or package.json change, so no slow deploy.
entries.concerns: Colours come from computed styles, so gradients and background images are not counted (on stripe.com the main colour came out green, not purple). A font whose CSS name differs from the name inside its file (stripe.com's sohne-var) is not matched, so only its name is kept. Chromium resolves names itself after the address check, so DNS rebinding is not fully covered (acceptable for a signed-in tool). A read takes 10 to 30 seconds and a few hundred MB of browser, at most 2 at once. Tried by hand on two real sites only. Not reachable from the app yet.

New serp_rankings table and a Tracked rankings section. Keywords gets a "New this period" filter.
entries.benefit: Fewer false "not ranked" answers, and rankings tracked over time without manual lookups.
entries.concerns: Spends money on DataForSEO (a real depth-30 search cost US$0.0018). It is off by default with an estimate and a monthly cap, but re-reads multiply the cost. A large change (27 files, 1,160 lines).

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Memory page: show the real error instead of "undefined memories stored"
entries.goal: Stop the Memory page saying "undefined memories stored" when something fails.
entries.whatChanged: load() used to store an error reply as if it were the list or the summary. A failing stats call now shows a red banner with the server's reason and the rest of the page keeps working; a failing list shows its error instead of crashing.
entries.benefit: A real, readable error instead of a confusing broken page.
entries.concerns: This shows the error but does not fix whatever made /api/memory/stats fail in the first place; the cause needs finding separately.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Memory: translate OCR pool on demand, memory log; SERP Tracker: Keywords tab (Search Console history)
entries.goal: Cut a high, spiky Railway memory bill, and add Search Console keyword history to the SERP Tracker.
entries.whatChanged: Translate's OCR pool is now built on first use, shut down after 5 idle minutes and defaults to 2 workers (it used to build 4 workers x 8 languages at every boot, about 575 MB of ~860 MB resting memory locally). New server/lib/memoryLog.js writes a line every 5 minutes with Node and container memory, and extra detail on a 300 MB jump. SERP Tracker gets a Keywords tab backed by Search Console history (16-month backfill, daily update at 7:00 am Brisbane, just-off-page-1 filter, per-keyword chart, slipped-keyword alerts).
entries.benefit: Lower and steadier hosting memory, a log that explains future spikes, and an early warning when keywords slip.
entries.concerns: The first translation after an idle period is slower while the OCR pool starts, and 2 workers may slow several OCR jobs at once. The memory saving was measured locally; the commit does not confirm the Railway bill has dropped. Two unrelated changes share one commit (23 files, 1,659 lines), which makes it harder to revert one without the other.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: SERP Tracker: "Use my location" and "Use Australia" for the search place
entries.goal: Make it easy to set the place a search is run from.
entries.whatChanged: "Use my location" reads the browser position, names the suburb through the shared geocoder and matches it to DataForSEO's place list; "Use Australia" resets it. It only fills the box and nothing saves until Save. An empty box still means Australia.
entries.benefit: Local-search results can match where the business actually is, without hunting for a place code.
entries.concerns: Needs the browser's location permission and the geocoder to answer; if the suburb does not match a DataForSEO place the person has to choose another.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: SERP Tracker: Google site setting (google.com.au) and a "Searching as" place label
entries.goal: Search the Australian Google index and show the real place used.
entries.whatChanged: Site setup gets a Google site setting (default google.com.au) sent as se_domain, plus a free check against DataForSEO's Australian place list that shows the place actually used (for example Bowen Hills, place 9060847). Docs record the LLM Search Cloud project for the Google OAuth client.
entries.benefit: Ranks should be closer to what a person on google.com.au sees, and the app is honest about the place it searched.
entries.concerns: This re-adds, as a setting, the se_domain idea that was reverted earlier the same day (d43297e8). The commit does not state that it fixed the gap between the tracker's page 2 and the real page 1, so that still needs checking against a real search.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Revert "SERP Tracker: send se_domain so Australia searches the google.com.au index"
entries.goal: Undo the automatic se_domain change from c27c23de.
entries.whatChanged: Reverts c27c23de, which always sent se_domain so Australia searched the google.com.au index.
entries.benefit: Returns the code to its previous known behaviour.
entries.concerns: The commit message does not say why it was reverted. The idea came back a few hours later as a visible setting (b43ef801).

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: SERP Tracker: send se_domain so Australia searches the google.com.au index
entries.goal: Fix ranks that differed from what a person on google.com.au sees.
entries.whatChanged: DataForSEO echoed se_domain google.com for location Australia, so a site on page 2 here was page 1 (#2) for a real user. The request now always sends se_domain so Australia searches the google.com.au index.
entries.benefit: Aimed to make tracked positions match real Australian results.
entries.concerns: Reverted by d43297e8 about 1.5 hours later, so it did not stay in. Always sending the domain for every site was probably too blunt, which the later setting (b43ef801) addresses.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: SERP Tracker: several sites (one per client), CRM client link, Find my site, honest coverage
entries.goal: Let one person track several sites (one per client) and find where a site ranks deep in the results.
entries.whatChanged: Up to 20 sites per person (each domain once) with a site switcher and Add/Delete with Undo (recycle bin type serp-site), an optional CRM client link, and a Quick lookup with no site. Find my site searches up to depth 200 with the expected cost shown first. Short pages from DataForSEO are recorded as coverage and retried (max 4) within the cost cap. A real queued-mode answer is kept as a parser fixture.
entries.benefit: Works for an agency with many clients, and tells the truth about how deep a search really read.
entries.concerns: Deep searches with retries are the most expensive thing in the tool (shown first and capped). One of the biggest commits in the set (27 files, about 1,970 lines added, 480 removed), so it carries more regression risk.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: SERP Tracker: keep the real Live answer as a parser fixture, with a test that reads it
entries.goal: Keep a real DataForSEO Live answer as a test fixture.
entries.whatChanged: Adds the real Live answer for "walk in wine cabinets" (Australia, desktop, top 10, AI summary on). serpParse.test.js now parses it against values read off it by hand. It holds only the search request and Google's public results, no credentials or account details.
entries.benefit: The parser is tested against a real answer rather than an invented one.
entries.concerns: None noted. A fixture is a snapshot, so it will not catch later changes in the real answer format.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: SERP Tracker Lookup: read real websites from Google redirect links, show ads and "searched as"
entries.goal: Stop the parser missing the owner's own site.
entries.whatChanged: A real Live answer showed most organic results as google.com/goto redirect links with domain google.com and the real site only in the breadcrumb, so the site could never be found. The parser now reads the site from the breadcrumb, says "not found but some results hide their website" rather than a flat not-ranked, lists sponsored ads (or says none came back) and shows what DataForSEO says it searched (Google site, place, language).
entries.benefit: Real rankings are found, and the result explains uncertainty instead of reporting a false miss.
entries.concerns: Depends on the shape of Google's results as relayed by DataForSEO, which can change. Older saved lookups say ads were not recorded.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: SERP Tracker: Lookup tab, saved lookups with select and delete, guide chat and info box
entries.goal: Add a Lookup tab so a single live search can be run and kept.
entries.whatChanged: Lookup runs a live DataForSEO search and parses position, boxes above, AI Overview citations, the top 10 and page layout. It logs the cost before parsing, honours the monthly cap and saves the result (latest 50, raw answer kept 90 days). Saved lookups can be opened, ticked and deleted through the shared recycle bin with Undo. Adds the SERP Tracker guide chat, (i) box and tooltips.
entries.benefit: A quick, costed way to see exactly how a keyword looks on Google today, with a history to look back on.
entries.concerns: Each lookup is a paid call. Raw answers are stored for 90 days, which adds database size.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: SERP Tracker stage 2: queued search calls and the depth cost test script
entries.goal: Add the cheaper queued search method and a script to measure its cost.
entries.whatChanged: postSerpTask, getSerpTask and waitForSerpTask for DataForSEO's Standard Queue with unit tests, DataForSEO's own message on 4xx errors, and server/scripts/serpDepthTest.js, a one-search cost test that never re-posts.
entries.benefit: A route to much lower per-search cost, and a safe way to find out what depth really costs.
entries.concerns: Not yet run against a real search when committed: DataForSEO answered 403 until the account was verified. Later commits show it working (depth 30 cost US$0.0018).

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: SERP Tracker stage 1: site profile, daily run, DataForSEO balance check, cost log
entries.goal: Start the SERP Tracker tool: site profile, a daily run and cost logging.
entries.whatChanged: New preview tool (flag serpTracker, off by default) at /serp-tracker. Saves the tracked site's settings, runs a daily job at 20:00 UTC (6 am Brisbane) that checks the DataForSEO balance and logs every call's cost, and records each run as ok or failed. The run engine takes independent modules so later stages plug in unchanged.
entries.benefit: Foundation for tracking search rankings with spend visible from day one.
entries.concerns: Introduces a scheduled job that calls a paid API; it runs under the cron single-flight lock and the tool is off by default. Stage 1 only checks the balance and logs costs, so it does not track rankings yet.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Usage page: info box, guide chat and tooltips
entries.goal: Give the Usage page the standard help set.
entries.whatChanged: Adds an info box, a Usage guide chat (route, service, registry entry and tests) and tooltips.
entries.benefit: The page explains itself and answers questions about where spend comes from.
entries.concerns: None noted. The commit has no message body beyond its title.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Usage page: modern layout and Advice tab on model choice
entries.goal: Modernise the Usage page and help choose cheaper models.
entries.whatChanged: New layout and an Advice tab on model choice, backed by a new usageInsights service and changes to the cost calculator and usage route.
entries.benefit: Spend is easier to read, and there is concrete guidance on which model to use for what.
entries.concerns: The advice is only as good as the usage data it reads, so its first suggestions are worth sanity-checking before acting. A large rewrite of the page (670 lines added, 262 removed) with no commit message explanation.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Web Extractor palette: group colours, show where each is used
entries.goal: Make the colour palette easier to read.
entries.whatChanged: Colours are grouped and the page shows where each one is used.
entries.benefit: The palette tells the designer where a colour matters, not only that it exists.
entries.concerns: None noted. The commit has no message body beyond its title.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Web Extractor palette: join near-identical shades, skip platform defaults, show main colours first
entries.goal: Cut noise from the palette result.
entries.whatChanged: Near-identical shades are joined, platform default colours are skipped and the main colours are shown first.
entries.benefit: A shorter, more useful list that reflects the brand rather than the framework.
entries.concerns: Joining near-identical shades uses a closeness threshold, so two colours meant to be different could be merged. The commit has no message body.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Web Extractor: add Colour palette tool
entries.goal: Add a tool that finds the colours a website uses.
entries.whatChanged: New Colour palette tool in the Page group. It counts colours from linked and imported style files, <style> blocks, style="" attributes and the theme-color meta, normalises them to #rrggbb, counts roles (background, text, border, other) and follows CSS variables and aliases. It suggests a primary, accent, background and text colour and splits brand colours from greys, whites and blacks. Optional "Pages to read" (1, 3 or 6). Swatches copy the hex, with Copy hex codes, Copy as CSS and Download CSV.
entries.benefit: Pulls a site's real colour scheme into a usable palette in seconds.
entries.concerns: Reading several pages means more requests to someone else's site, though they go through the app's existing safe-fetch checks and each page is fetched once. The "one page only" wording elsewhere now has this exception.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Domain page: pick up names in single quotes, add spotted names automatically
entries.goal: Recognise names the person puts in single quotes and add them automatically.
entries.whatChanged: Anything in double, curly or single quotes counts as a name (a single quote only when it opens a word, so apostrophes are safe). Names spotted in the description are added to "Names I already have" when Generate is pressed, unless removed with the x on their chip. The brief shows a tip about the quotes rule.
entries.benefit: Less retyping, and names the person already chose are built into the suggestions.
entries.concerns: A quoted phrase that is not a name could be added. It can be removed with the chip's x. This reverses the previous commit's "never added automatically".

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Domain page: use the names you mention, and talk the names through
entries.goal: Build domain suggestions around names the person already has and let them talk the names through.
entries.whatChanged: Names spotted in the description (a book called X, an artist named Y, quoted titles, runs of capitalised words) are offered as one-click "Names I already have". Names are built around those: ownCombos joins the title or person with the brief's words, and candidates built on an own name rank first and are not penalised. "Talk it through" adds a question box (POST /api/domains/ask, answered from the names and their checks, changes nothing) and a notes box that triggers a new round. The last 12 turns are saved with the set.
entries.benefit: Suggestions reflect the person's own names, and they can ask why or refine the brief without starting over.
entries.concerns: A new AI route (ask) that costs per question. The ranking change favours own-name candidates, so check the results are not crowded by them. A large commit (26 files).

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Domain generation: stop long rounds timing out
entries.goal: Stop long domain-generation rounds timing out.
entries.whatChanged: The wide list is now written by two AI calls at once (about 90 names each, 150 s each) instead of one call for 180 names; one failing is fine, both timing out gives a clear 504 telling the person to try again or pick a faster model. Every DomScan request times out after 20 s. A time budget per round: no new domain lookup starts after 170 s and explanations are skipped past 200 s, so a slow AI step cannot push the request past the hosting gateway limit.
entries.benefit: Generation finishes or fails clearly instead of hanging until the gateway cuts it off.
entries.concerns: On a slow round the time budget means fewer availability checks and no explanations, so a round can return a thinner list. Two parallel AI calls double the call count for each round.
